results: 1. observation of the jerks: periodic myoclonus with a SLOW relaxation phase involving bilateral shoulder abductors and hip flexors
2. anti-measles antibody titres (serum): raised, with CSF-restricted synthesis
3. EEG: periodic slow wave complexes TIME-LOCKED to the myoclonic jerks
4. lumbar puncture / CSF: intrathecal synthesis of anti-measles IgG
5. measles vaccination and infection history: measles in infancy; SSPE typically follows 4-12 years later, but onset here was in adulthood
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Adult-onset subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE) caused by persistent measles virus infection following childhood measles

Alternative 1: Sporadic Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease

Alternative 2: Progressive myoclonic epilepsy

Alternative 3: Autoimmune encephalitis with myoclonus
dx: Adult-onset subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE) caused by persistent measles virus infection following childhood measles
